output.entity_proposed: Dental Unit in every Rural Health Unit
output.proposal: HB No. 10993, the proposed Local Dental Health Unit Act, seeks to create a dental unit, composed of a public health dentist and a trained Barangay Health Worker as dental aide, in every rural health unit under the supervision of the Department of Health (DOH), to promote preventive dental health care in rural areas as part of the Primary Health Care Approach.
output.alignment: As a measure on government organization and mandates, the review should examine how the proposed dental units fit with the existing structure of rural health units and the DOH, including the respective roles of the DOH and local government units under Section 4 (Creation of a Dental Unit in every Rural Health Unit) and Section 5 (Implementing Rules and Regulations), and how the measure relates to the government's intent to streamline the Executive branch and reduce overlapping functions under the Government Optimization Act (RA No. 12231). The measure aligns with the Human Capital Development priority area of the FY 2027 Budget Priorities Framework, particularly its focus on the Universal Health Care system. It is not among the measures in the LEDAC Common Legislative Agenda.
legislative_history: HB No. 10993 was filed on August 26, 2026 by Representative Patrick Michael "PM" D. Vargas; its current status is filed (pending), and later stages are not yet reflected in available records.

Bills bearing the same title were filed in the 18th Congress (HB Nos. 387, 1267, 1367, 3618, 5232, 5787 and 10391; SB No. 962) and the 19th Congress (HB Nos. 1487, 2520, 3986, 5095 and 9343; SB No. 636); their texts have not been compared with HB No. 10993.
SB No. 1194, filed in the Senate on August 14, 2025 under a matching title, is pending in the Committee and may be considered the counterpart measure.
HB No. 11468, also filed in the 20th Congress, proposes the same Local Dental Health Unit Act with a revised design for the dental units.

output.salient_features:
HB No. 10993, to be known as the Local Dental Health Unit Act, seeks to create a dental unit in every rural health unit under the supervision of the Department of Health. Its salient features are as follows:
a. Section 2 (Declaration of Policy) provides that the State shall pursue the Primary Health Care Approach in the delivery of health services, undertake related human resource development and promote preventive dental health care in rural areas.
b. Section 3 (Definition of Terms) defines a rural health unit as the main health center, composed of a doctor, a nurse and a midwife, that carries out the DOH's preventive and curative public health functions, and defines a dental unit as composed of a public health dentist and a trained Barangay Health Worker serving as dental aide.
c. Section 4 (Creation of a Dental Unit in every Rural Health Unit) provides that a dental unit shall be created in every rural health unit, under DOH supervision, as part of the Primary Health Care Approach; no salary grades or plantilla positions are specified.
d. Section 5 (Implementing Rules and Regulations) provides that the DOH, in coordination with local government units, shall issue the implementing rules within six months of the Act's effectivity.
e. Section 6 (Funding) provides that initial implementation shall be charged against the DOH's current-year appropriation, and that funding thereafter shall be included in the annual General Appropriations Act.
f. Section 7 (Separability Clause), Section 8 (Repealing Clause) and Section 9 (Effectivity) contain the standard closing provisions, with the Act taking effect fifteen days after publication.
output.related_measures_policy: HB No. 10993 may be considered alongside its Senate counterpart, SB No. 1194, and HB No. 11468, which proposes the same Local Dental Health Unit Act but places the dental units in rural health units operated by local government units, with minimum staffing subject to civil service and budgetary rules and with the DOH providing standards and technical assistance. Bills on the same subject were filed in the 18th and 19th Congresses, together with proposals for a rural dentist position and for dental services in city or municipal health units. The measure aligns with the Human Capital Development priority under the FY 2027 Budget Priorities Framework, particularly the Universal Health Care system. The review should assess the supervision arrangement under Section 4 (Creation of a Dental Unit in every Rural Health Unit) against the coordination role of local government units under Section 5 (Implementing Rules and Regulations), the possible overlap with the dental health functions indicated by the title of RA No. 3814, the number of public health dentist and dental aide positions implied by Section 3 (Definition of Terms), and the fit of the new units with streamlining under the Government Optimization Act (RA No. 12231).

fiscal_requirements.detail: Amount necessary for initial implementation, charged against the DOH's current-year appropriation; no amount stated

reviewer_checks: Confirm whether rural health units are under DOH supervision or operated by local government units, as Section 4 places the dental units under DOH supervision while Section 5 requires coordination with local government units.
Note that the bill title refers to the 'Primary Approach' while Sections 2 and 4 refer to the Primary Health Care Approach; check for a possible omission in the title.
Check the wording of Section 3 (Definition of Terms), where the rural health unit definition reads 'Its function to carry out', which appears to omit a word.
The composition of the dental unit appears only in Section 3 (Definition of Terms); confirm whether the positions are intended to be created and at what salary grade.
Confirm the status of SB No. 1194 with the Senate and compare the text of HB No. 11468, which proposes a different staffing and supervision arrangement.
Confirm the number of rural health units nationwide to estimate the cost of the dentist and dental aide positions and equipment.
